claim_formal: ∀ smooth complete intersection X ⊂ ℙ^N_ℂ: L_k^X Z_X = 0 for all k ≥ −1 (all genera, curve classes, insertions in H*(X;ℂ))

quote_A.text: Its ordinary, unreduced total descendant potential satisfies the Virasoro constraints in every genus and curve class, with arbitrary insertions from H^*(X;ℂ).

quote_B.text: We prove the Virasoro conjecture for the ordinary descendant Gromov–Witten theory of smooth complete intersections in projective space

notes: Virasoro conjecture is posed for all smooth projective varieties; settled for the class of projective complete intersections (O5). Second result: V(B) ⇒ V(P_B(E)) for any vector bundle of rank ≥2 (transfer theorem, M1), giving projective-bundle towers.

claim_formal: ∀ d ∈ ℕ_{>0}, ε ∈ ℚ_{>0} ∃ N = N(d,ε) ∀ ε-lc Fano contraction f: X → Z of dim d over alg. closed char-0 k, ∀ closed z ∈ Z ∃ B ≥ 0, U ∋ z: (X,B) klt over U ∧ N(K_X+B)|_{f^{-1}U} ~ 0

quote_A.text: admits, near each closed base point, a klt complement of index bounded only by d and ϵ

quote_B.text: This proves the finite-rational-coefficient form of Shokurov's bounded-klt-complement conjecture.

notes: Matrix is a uniform-boundedness statement (existence of a complement with index ≤ N(d,ε)); M8 chosen over M2 because the content is the uniform bound; constant explicitly non-effective. O1 vs O5: the proved form is the finite-rational-coefficient form (Chen's Conj. 1.1 formulation); other (real/hyperstandard) forms may remain. Relies on Chen's equivalence with local thresholds. Third manuscript proves Birkar–Shokurov Cartier-divisor conjecture. Lean comparator is a compactness lemma about a closed-chart field retraction (intermediate).

claim_formal: ∀ smooth connected complex projective Fano X with dim X = 6: T_X nef → X ≅ G/P rational homogeneous

quote_A.text: Every smooth connected complex projective Fano variety of dimension six with nef tangent bundle is rational homogeneous.

quote_B.text: resolving the Campana–Peternell conjecture in complex dimension six

notes: Uses Kanemitsu (ρ>n−5) and Watanabe to reduce to Picard number one, pseudoindex 4/5. Corollary: uniformization of compact Kähler manifolds with nef tangent bundle and dim − q̃ ≤ 6.

claim_formal: ∀ smooth connected complex projective X: (−K_X admits a smooth semipositive Hermitian metric) → ∃ m > 0: H^0(X, −mK_X) ≠ 0

quote_A.text: If −K_X admits a smooth Hermitian metric of semipositive curvature, then H^0(X,−mK_X)≠0 for some integer m>0.

quote_B.text: This is the positive-multiple formulation associated with Yau's anticanonical nonvanishing question [Problem 75, p. 395]

notes: Problem source is Yau's numbered problem list (Problem 75), hence P3; outcome O1 for the positive-multiple formulation (paper frames it as the formulation 'associated with' Yau's question; the first-power version is false by the Enriques×ℙ¹ example). Family has 7 manuscripts with auxiliary results (invariant anticanonical index polynomiality, pseudoeffective-error conversion, klt-pair nonvanishing).

claim_formal: ∀ connected simple complex G, ∀ smooth projective connected complex curve X, ∀ c ∈ ℂ∖ℚ: D_c(Bun_G(X)) ≃ D_{−1/(rc)}(Bun_{G^∨}(X)) as presentable ℂ-linear DG categories

quote_A.text: For every c∈ℂ∖ℚ there is an equivalence of presentable ℂ-linear DG categories D_c(Bun_G(X)) ≃ D_{−1/(rc)}(Bun_{G^∨}(X)).

quote_B.text: Theorem gives its unramified de Rham equivalence in the irrational range.

notes: Quantum geometric Langlands conjecture (Stoyanovsky/Drinfeld, Gaitsgory; Bogdanova–Betti Conj. 1) settled for irrational levels only (rational levels excluded), unramified de Rham setting. Relies heavily on the proof of ordinary GLC and Campbell–Dhillon–Raskin local equivalences.

claim_formal: ∀ nonempty connected open G ⊂ Ĉ ∃ circle domain V ∃ conformal equivalence f: G → V

quote_A.text: Every nonempty connected open set G⊂Ĉ is conformally equivalent to a circle domain.

quote_B.text: resolving Koebe's circle-domain conjecture positively

notes: Existence part of Koebe's Kreisnormierungsproblem. Second manuscript: circle domains with conformally removable boundary are rigid (removability-to-rigidity direction of He–Schramm conjecture; other direction already refuted by Rajala). Lean has both koebe_circle_domain and removability_implies_rigidity.

claim_formal: ∀ simply connected W ⊊ ℂ (≥2 boundary points in Ĉ), ∀ conformal bijection φ: W → 𝔻, ∀ s ∈ (4/3, 4): ∫_W |φ'|^s dA < ∞

quote_A.text: Every conformal bijection φ:W→𝔻 satisfies ∫_W|φ'(z)|^s dA(z)<∞ (4/3<s<4).

quote_B.text: We prove Brennan's conjecture

notes: Also B_S(−2)=1 and B_S(t)=|t|−1 for t≤−2 (M9), Koebe sharpness of endpoints. Second manuscript: B_b(−1)<1/4 disproves Kraetzer's conjectured spectrum (M3/O2 for that conjecture). Lean MainStatement covers uniform bound, B_S(−2)=1 and Brennan integrability.

claim_formal: ∀ d ≥ 2, ∀ compact E ⊂ ℝ^d: dim_H E > d/2 → 𝓛¹(Δ(E)) > 0

quote_A.text: Let d≥2 be an integer and let E⊂ℝ^d be compact. If dim_H E>d/2, then 𝓛¹(Δ(E))>0.

quote_B.text: We resolve the Falconer distance conjecture in every dimension.

notes: Lean FalconerAllDimensions matches; separate PlanarFalconer comparator is the d=2 special case.

quote_A.text: the maximal average over unit tubes of radius δ maps L³(ℝ³) to L³(S²) with norm at most C_ε δ^{−ε}

quote_B.text: We prove the Kakeya maximal conjecture in three dimensions.

notes: Kakeya maximal conjecture is posed in all dimensions n; settled for n=3 (O5). Builds on Wang–Zahl's 3D set theorem / Guth–Wang–Zahl. Second headline: every Kakeya set in ℝ⁴ has Hausdorff dimension 4 (∀, M9/M1, P1, O5). Prefix treats the constant C_ε as part of the bound, not a main object.

claim_formal: ∀ f ∈ L log L(𝕋), for a.e. x ∈ 𝕋: S_N f(x) → f(x) as N → ∞

quote_A.text: For every complex-valued f∈L log L(𝕋), there is a measurable set N_f of measure zero such that lim_{N→∞} S_N f(x)=f(x)

quote_B.text: This establishes the classical L log L sufficiency conjecture.

notes: Prefix: ∀ over f, then almost-every x (rule 3) though x is arguably not a main object; a plain '∀' reading is also defensible. Corollary: Luxemburg weak-L¹ maximal bound.

quote_A.text: there is a polynomial of length N with coefficients in {−1,1} whose modulus lies between (1−ε)√N and (1+ε)√N everywhere on the unit circle

quote_B.text: Their binary merit factors tend to infinity, disproving Turyn's bounded-merit-factor conjecture.

notes: Existence construction whose family refutes Turyn's bounded-merit-factor conjecture and the real-sign analogue of Erdős's fixed relative-gap question (Erdős 1957 Problem 22; could be P3), so M3 over M2. Outcome could be read as O3 (refutes gap conjecture and determines lim m_N = 1, rule 7). Ultraflat manuscript explicitly builds on two earlier OpenAI manuscripts. Lean (AsymptoticallyMinimalLittlewood) has only the upper bound (1+η)√N, not the lower bound: weaker. N_0 non-explicit.

claim_formal: ∀ compact smooth positively curved surface Σ ⊂ ℝ³ (possibly with boundary), ∀ p ∈ (3,∞) ∃ C_{Σ,p} ∀ f ∈ L^p(Σ): ‖E_Σ f‖_{L^p(ℝ³)} ≤ C ‖f‖_{L^p(Σ)}

quote_A.text: For every 3<p<∞, the extension operator maps L^p(Σ) boundedly into L^p(ℝ³).

quote_B.text: We prove the diagonal Fourier extension conjecture for compact smooth positively curved surfaces Σ⊂ℝ³

notes: Boundedness in the full conjectured open range (sharp threshold p=3 known), so M9 also defensible; M1 chosen as the claim is operator boundedness, no endpoint. Restriction conjecture is posed in every dimension; this is the 3D positively-curved case (O5; O1 if the 3D conjecture is read as its own problem). Uses the OpenAI packet propagation theorem (companion sphere bounded-data manuscript). Corollaries: 2D Schrödinger local smoothing, Kakeya maximal in 3D.

claim_formal: ∀ p ∈ [1,∞], ∀ δ > max{3|1/p − 1/2| − 1/2, 0}: T_δ = (1−|ξ|²)_+^δ multiplier is bounded on L^p(ℝ³)

quote_A.text: The main result is boundedness of the Bochner–Riesz multipliers on L³(ℝ³) for every positive order.

quote_B.text: We prove the three-dimensional Bochner–Riesz conjecture in its strict-order formulation.

notes: Bochner–Riesz conjecture posed in all dimensions; 3D case settled (O5; strict range, endpoint not addressed). Operator boundedness coded M1; M9 (sharp threshold) arguable since necessity is classical.

claim_formal: ∀ ε > 0 ∃ C_ε ∀ f ∈ 𝒮(ℝ³): ‖e^{it√−Δ} f‖_{L³(ℝ³×[1,2])} ≤ C_ε ‖J^ε f‖_{L³(ℝ³)} (hence local smoothing for all 2<p<∞, α > max{0,1−3/p})

quote_A.text: We prove the critical L3 local smoothing estimate for the wave equation in three spatial dimensions, with every positive Sobolev loss.

quote_B.text: This resolves Sogge's Euclidean local smoothing conjecture in dimension three.

notes: A priori estimate with ε-loss coded M1 (operator boundedness, no rate); M8 is a defensible alternative. Sogge's conjecture is posed for all dimensions; 3D case (O5). Strict range only, lossless endpoint not addressed. Corollaries: wave maximal estimates and Bochner–Riesz maximal bounds in ℝ³.

claim_formal: ∀ n ≥ 2, ∀ f ∈ H^{n/(2(n+1))}(ℝ^n), for a.e. x ∈ ℝ^n: lim_{t↓0} e^{itΔ} f(x) = f(x)

quote_A.text: For initial data in H^{n/(2(n+1))}(ℝ^n), the free Schrödinger evolution converges almost everywhere to the initial data as t↓0.

quote_B.text: Bourgain's later counterexample forces s ≥ n/[2(n+1)] when n≥2, but does not rule out equality.

notes: Posed problem: the endpoint (equality) case of Carleson's pointwise convergence problem, open with no predicted answer stated (P2); answered affirmatively in all n≥2. With Bourgain's necessity this determines the exact threshold including the endpoint (M9 arguable). Higher-dimensional manuscript reuses lemmas of the planar OpenAI companion.

claim_formal: ∀ d ≥ 4, 2 ≤ n ≤ d−2, ∀ n-ADR Radon measure μ on ℝ^d: (n-dim Riesz transform uniformly L²(μ)-bounded over hard truncations) → μ uniformly n-rectifiable, with constants θ, M depending only on d, n, C_AD, C_R

quote_A.text: an n-Ahlfors–David regular Radon measure on ℝd is uniformly n-rectifiable if its n-dimensional Riesz transform is uniformly bounded

quote_B.text: This gives a positive answer to the David–Semmes Riesz-transform question in its remaining higher-codimension range.

notes: Lean is quantitative ∀(d,n,C_AD,C_R) ∃(θ,M) ∀μ; prefix given over the main object μ (∀), with uniform constants as part of the conclusion. Settles the remaining range 2≤n≤d−2; n=1 (MMV/Farag) and n=d−1 (Nazarov–Tolsa–Volberg) were known, so the full David–Semmes question follows only with prior results (O1 + flag; O5 if only this paper's range is counted).

claim_formal: ∀ r > 2 ∃ C_r ∀ F, G ∈ L³(ℝ²; ℂ): ‖V_r(F,G)‖_{L^{3/2}} ≤ C_r ‖F‖_3 ‖G‖_3 (annular r-variation of the triangular Hilbert transform; implies maximal bound and symmetric L³×L³×L³ trilinear form bound)

quote_A.text: We prove the annular r-variation estimate for the triangular Hilbert transform from complex L3×L3 to L3/2 for every r>2.

quote_B.text: In particular, the result resolves positively the symmetric triangular Hilbert transform problem stated by Thiele in [Section 9, Problem 13].

notes: Problem source: Thiele's Problem 13 in a numbered problem collection (Grafakos et al. 2017), hence P3. Settled at the symmetric exponent point only; if Problem 13 is read as the full range of exponents, O5. restricted_range = symmetric L³ point. Lean states only the two-endpoint maximal estimate (single-increment special case of the variation bound): weaker. Third manuscript: absolute L³ bound (constant 40) for the dyadic model.

claim_formal: ∃ absolute a_* ∈ (0,1/2), C_* < ∞ ∀ Lipschitz v: ℝ² → S¹ with Lip(v) ≤ 1, ∀ ε ∈ (0,a_*), ∀ f ∈ 𝒮(ℝ²): ‖H^ε_{v,a_*} f‖_2 ≤ C_* ‖f‖_2 (hence weak-(2,2) for the principal value)

quote_A.text: We prove a uniform L2 bound for the Hilbert transform along a Lipschitz unit vector field in the plane, with integration restricted to a fixed absolute multiple of the reciprocal Lipschitz seminorm.

quote_B.text: This gives an affirmative answer to Stein's weak-(2,2) conjecture.

notes: Prefix follows the Lean (∃ a C ∀ v …): the absolute scale a_* is part of the headline. Uniform operator bound coded M1 (M8 arguable). Stein's conjecture as formulated by Lacey–Li (Conj. 1.5) has exactly this short-scale form, so O1 (summary's 'at this short scale' suggests O5 is also a reading).

quote_A.text: there is a compact set E_{q,η}⊆[0,1] with m(E_{q,η})>1−η such that for every x∈ℝ and s∈ℝ∖{0}, x+sq^n∉E_{q,η} for some integer n≥1.

quote_B.text: We prove the geometric-progression case of the Erdős similarity conjecture.

notes: Equivalently G_q is not measure universal (M4 reading). Erdős similarity conjecture also appears as Problem 4.33.7* in Erdős's problem list (P3 arguable). Only the class of geometric progressions is settled (O5). Lean covers only q=1/2 (dyadic case): weaker.

claim_formal: ∃ C < ∞ ∀ real f ∈ W^{1,1}(ℝ²): Mf ∈ W^{1,1}_loc(ℝ²) ∧ ‖∇Mf‖_1 ≤ C ‖∇f‖_1 (M = centered disk maximal operator)

quote_A.text: We prove the endpoint gradient bound ‖∇Mf‖_1≤C‖∇f‖_1 for every real-valued f∈W^{1,1}(ℝ²)

quote_B.text: This gives a positive resolution of the planar centered-disk case of the endpoint question of Hajłasz and Onninen.

notes: Hajłasz–Onninen Question 1 is posed in all dimensions; planar centered case settled (O5). Absolute constant C treated as part of the bound; Lean writes ∃C ∀f. A second Lean comparator (SignedFiniteBand) is an intermediate proposition.

quote_A.text: We prove that the trilinear Hilbert transform with fixed slopes 1, 2, 3 maps L3(ℝ)×L3(ℝ)×L3(ℝ) to L1(ℝ)

quote_B.text: The full conjecture asks for a broader range of exponents; see [Conjecture 1.7].

notes: Single exponent point (L³×L³×L³→L¹) of the trilinear Hilbert transform conjecture, fixed slopes 1,2,3: O5. Uses Leng–Sah–Sawhney inverse theorem.

claim_formal: ∀ n ≥ 1, ∀ origin-symmetric convex body K ⊂ ℝ^n: |K|·|K°| ≥ 4^n/n!, with equality ⇔ K is a linear image of a Hanner polytope

quote_A.text: Every origin-symmetric convex body in ℝn has volume product at least 4^n/n!, with equality exactly for invertible linear images of Hanner polytopes.

quote_B.text: We resolve the symmetric Mahler conjecture positively, including its equality classification.

notes: Family also proves the nonsymmetric Mahler conjecture (P(K) ≥ (n+1)^{n+1}/(n!)², equality iff simplex), functional Mahler inequalities, and Gromov width of K×K° equal to 4 for n≥2 (separate symplectic proof of the symmetric inequality). Lean comparators cover symmetric inequality, its equality case, general Mahler and polar-product width.

claim_formal: ∀ n ≥ 4, ∀ convex body K ⊂ ℝ^n: |ΠK|/|K|^{n−1} ≥ κ_{n−1}^n κ_n^{2−n}, with equality ⇔ K is an ellipsoid

quote_A.text: We prove that ellipsoids uniquely minimize the volume of the projection body among convex bodies of fixed volume in every dimension at least four.

quote_B.text: Combining it with the separately proved three-dimensional theorem of Chen et al. establishes the conjecture for every n≥3

notes: Petty's projection-volume conjecture (n≥3): this family proves n≥4; n=3 by Chen–Feng–Li–Xi–Xu, so the full conjecture holds only with prior results (O1 + flag; O5 if counted per paper). Second result: T10×T10 counterexample to Brannen's simplex-maximum conjecture (M3/O2; already refuted for d≥9 by Feng–Hu–Liu–Xu) with exponential excess. Lutwak–Petty projection inequalities also claimed in summary.

claim_formal: ∃ C ≥ 1 ∀ finite connected planar G, ∀ ℓ: E → (0,∞) ∃ f: V → L_1: d_G(x,y) ≤ ‖f(x)−f(y)‖_1 ≤ C d_G(x,y) ∀ x,y

quote_A.text: There is a finite universal constant C≥1 with the following property. For every finite connected planar graph G=(V,E) with strictly positive real edge lengths, there exist a measure space … and a map f

quote_B.text: This resolves the bounded-treewidth case of the Gupta–Newman–Rabinovich–Sinclair conjecture positively.

notes: Content is the uniform distortion bound (M8; M2 for the embedding is an alternative). GNRS conjecture is for all proper minor-closed families; planar and bounded-treewidth cases settled (O5). Bounded-treewidth theorem: ∀k ∃C_k ∀G … (non-explicit C_k). Corollary: uniformly bounded multicommodity flow–cut gaps. Lean has both planar and treewidth statements.

claim_formal: ∀ smooth nonnegative completely monotone g on (0,∞), ∀ locally finite C ⊂ ℝ² of centered disk density one: E_g(C) ≥ E_g(A_△) (triangular lattice of covolume 1)

quote_A.text: it minimizes the lower limit of centered-ball energy averages for every nonnegative completely monotone function of squared distance

quote_B.text: Their Euclidean conjecture singled out the triangular, E_8, and Leech lattices [Conjecture 9.4].

notes: Universal optimality of the triangular lattice (planar case of Cohn–Kumar Conj. 9.4; E8/Leech done by CKMRV). Minimum value attained by the lattice, so M9 (minimizers not classified). Also proves Sandier–Serfaty conjecture (Coulomb renormalized energy), 2D Brauchart–Hardin–Saff linear term, Riesz 0<s<2, and planar Cohn–Elkies sharpness (sharp Fourier certificate, interval arithmetic).

claim_formal: ∀ n ≥ 1, ∀ origin-symmetric convex bodies K, L ⊂ ℝ^n, ∀ λ ∈ [0,1]: |𝒲[h_K^{1−λ} h_L^λ]| ≥ |K|^{1−λ} |L|^λ

quote_A.text: For every 0≤λ≤1, |𝒲[h_K^{1−λ}h_L^λ]| ≥ |K|^{1−λ}|L|^λ.

quote_B.text: We prove the logarithmic Brunn–Minkowski conjecture for arbitrary origin-symmetric convex bodies in every dimension.

notes: Conjecture of Böröczky–Lutwak–Yang–Zhang (Problem 1.1 in their paper). Stancu announced the result earlier with deferred details; not treated as a prior proof. Corollaries: symmetric L_p Brunn–Minkowski for 0<p<1, log-BM for even log-concave measures and the (B)-conjecture via Saroglou's transfer.

claim_formal: ∃ c, C > 0 ∀^∞ n: c n log n ≤ sup_K θ(K) ≤ C n log n, for θ = θ_L and θ = θ_T, over all and over centrally symmetric convex bodies K ⊂ ℝ^n

quote_A.text: Determines the optimal worst-case covering density as Θ(n log n), for both lattice and unrestricted translative coverings.

quote_B.text: Theorem removes this remaining iterated-logarithmic loss and gives the constant-factor n log n bound.

notes: Two halves: lattice upper bound C n log n for every body (improves Li–Liu record n log n (log log n)^{…}) and translative lower bound c n log n for symmetric bodies (answers Naszódi's universal-linear-bound question negatively, P2/O2). Combined, the order is determined (rule 7: O1 with M9, up to absolute constants). Lean CoveringOrder.optimal_order matches the combined statement.

claim_formal: ∃ C < ∞ ∀ n ≥ 1, ∀ centered log-concave μ with density on ℝ^n, ∀ a > 0 (μ linearly a-subgaussian), ∀ f ∈ C_c^∞: Ent_μ(f²) ≤ C a² ∫ |Df|² dμ

quote_A.text: satisfies Ent_μ(f^2) ≤ Ca^2∫|Df|^2 dμ for compactly supported smooth f, with one universal constant C

quote_B.text: This resolves positively the dimension-free logarithmic Sobolev conjecture for subgaussian log-concave measures.

notes: Dimension-free universal constant is the content, so ∃C outermost and M8 (bound on the LSI constant); M1 also readable. Bizeul's Conjecture 2. Corollary: Talagrand transport–entropy inequality with the same constant. Explicitness of C not stated.

quote_A.text: every n-point subset of a real Lp space embeds into ℓ_p^d with distortion at most D and subpolynomial dimension d=n^{o(1)}

quote_B.text: answering Naor's sublinear-dimension question for p ≠ 2

notes: Prefix keeps ∃C_{p,D} since the rate exp(C(log n)^γ) is the claim (could also be read as ∀ with an asymptotic rate). Also exact embeddings need dimension Θ(n²) (M9), and log n lower bound. Upper exponent not claimed optimal.

claim_formal: ∃ real homogeneous hyperbolic polynomial p (w.r.t. e): K(p,e) is not a spectrahedral shadow (no finite affine semidefinite lift with any number of auxiliary variables)

quote_A.text: There exists a real homogeneous hyperbolic polynomial whose closed hyperbolicity cone has no finite semidefinite lift.

quote_B.text: This disproves the Projected Lax Conjecture and hence the generalized Lax conjecture.

notes: Projected Lax Conjecture (Netzer–Sanyal) refuted; existence argument in high dimension, no explicit witness. Lean (main_result) formalizes the explicit degree-20, 23-variable cone that is not spectrahedral, i.e. the secondary refutation of the generalized Lax conjecture; that explicit cone does admit a semidefinite lift (third manuscript), so the Lean covers a different, weaker result.

claim_formal: ∀ d, k ≥ 1, ∀ measurable partition (A_1,…,A_k) of ℝ^d: Σ_i ‖∫_{A_i} x dγ_d‖² ≤ 9/(8π), with equality attained by the 2π/3 propeller for d ≥ 2, k ≥ 3

quote_A.text: for every finite measurable partition of a Euclidean space, the sum of the squared lengths of its Gaussian first moments is at most 9/(8π)

quote_B.text: We prove the Gaussian propeller conjecture

notes: Uses Heilman–Jagannath–Naor's ℝ³ theorem (four-cell case) as input and Khot–Naor's conical reduction. Corollary: NP-hardness (under the separate UG theorem) of improving the (8π/9)(1−1/k) kernel clustering factor.
